newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon trade union poll elects two leaders.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon trade union poll elects two leaders.

text.p: Voting to choose a head for Lebanon's General Labour Confederation ended in division on Thursday with the election of two union leaderships -- one pro-government and one leftist.
In a morning electoral session, the union's current leader Elias Abu Rizk was re-elected for a second four-year term at the union's headquarters in Beirut.
Police, throwing a heavy cordon around the building, banned journalists and trade union observers from attending the vote.
"Some 27 union delegates out of a 44-member electoral body attended the session and voted for my list," Abu Rizk told reporters outside the building.

Abu Rizk accused the government of interfering in the elections by not recognising the first vote and sponsoring another one in the afternoon in which government loyalist Ghneim al-Zoghbi was elected as chief of the trade union.
The second round of elections was held under the observation of a labour ministry representative.
Zoghbi told reporters that 35 out of a 54-member electoral body participated in the election and that he got 33 votes.
"My difficult task will be to unite the General Labour Confederation, if I cannot fulfill this mission I will resign," said al-Zoghbi, who unexpectedly entered Abu Rizk's office.

Abu Rizk shook hands with Zoghbi saying: "If you are addressing me under the title of head of the confederation, then let me remind you that your elections are illegal and were held under repression".
State-run Lebanese television Teleliban quoted Labour Minister Assad Hardan as saying that the government recognised only one election, that of Zoghbi.
